newsitem.title: USA: Lilly Industries sees higher FY96 oper net.
newsitem.headline: Lilly Industries sees higher FY96 oper net.

text.p: Lilly Industries Inc said Monday it expects operating profits for fiscal 1996 will exceed those of a year ago, excluding a one-time restructuring expense of $9.6 million incurred in the second quarter.
That expense related to the acquisition of Guardsman Products Inc in April.

In a statement, Douglas Huemme, chairman, said the company was particularly pleased with progress made in integrating the Guardsman business. He said "redundant costs" of about $15 million on an annual basis have already been cut from the operations of the combined companies.
"This rapid elimination of redundant costs was the principal reason Guardsman made a positive contribution to Lilly's overall earnings after just five months of Lilly's ownership," Huemme said.

He added that Lilly's original expectations to cut at least $20 million from operating expenses of the combined companies over the next 12 month to 24 months was proving to be conservative. Huemme said cost reductions of at least $25 million was "more probable."
"We expect to see a continuing increase in profitability during the final three months of our fiscal year," Huemme said.

Lilly also said it purchased a powder coatings manufacturing plant located at University Research Park in Charlotte, N.C. The company said the new plant gives it the capacity to roughly double its powder coatings sales.
"Powder coatings is our fastest growing product line, and the opportunity to expand this business is strategic to our growth plans," Huemme said.
Earlier, Lilly reported third quarter earnings of $0.30 a share, up from $0.20 a year ago.
Lilly makes industrial coatings and specialty chemicals.
